prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1136; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record today. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving through an intersection in Pearland, Texas. I had been heading toward a shopping center and was turning left.

Q: What was the traffic like at the time?

A: It was fairly light. There were a couple of cars coming the other way, and I waited for a gap before I started my turn.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not clearly. I saw headlights, but I didn't register how fast it was moving until it was already on me.

Q: How would you describe the impact?

A: It was a hard jolt from the side. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. The airbags didn't deploy, but my seatbelt locked up and I felt it across my chest.

Q: Did you feel any pain right away?

A: Not immediately. I felt shaken, and I was sore by the end of that evening. By the next morning the stiffness in my neck was hard to ignore.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic the following day, and then my primary care doctor referred me to physical therapy.

Q: Describe the treatment you've received since.

A: I've been doing physical therapy about twice a week. They've had me work on range of motion and strengthening the muscles around my neck and upper back. I also use a heating pad at home and take anti-inflammatory medication when the pain flares up.

Q: How has your neck pain affected your daily life?

A: It affects a lot of things. Driving for more than thirty minutes is uncomfortable, and I've had to stop lifting my grandchildren the way I used to. I also have trouble sleeping on my left side, and I've missed some time at the gym I used to go to regularly.

Q: Have you returned to your normal work duties?

A: I have, but some days I need to take short breaks to stretch, and I can't sit at my desk for long stretches the way I could before the accident.

Q: Do you have any prior neck problems?

A: I had occasional stiffness from sitting at a computer, but nothing that required a doctor's visit or treatment before this accident.
